rubrics.name: A short answer about a text

levels.Beginning: With help, gives an answer that is about the passage but not about the question asked.
levels.Developing: Gives an answer to the question that is partly right or misses one of its key points.
levels.Secure: Gives an answer that matches every key point the question needs.
levels.Extending: Gives every key point and adds a reason of their own that fits the passage.

levels.Beginning: Gives no detail from the passage, or a detail that does not fit.
levels.Developing: Gives one detail from the passage in their own words.
levels.Secure: Gives a detail or a short quote from the passage that supports the answer.
levels.Extending: Gives two or more details or quotes and says how each supports the answer.

rubrics.name: A sentence written or rewritten to a brief

levels.Beginning: Writes a sentence, but without the change that was asked for.
levels.Developing: Makes the change asked for, but the sentence reads awkwardly or changes its meaning.
levels.Secure: Makes the change asked for and keeps the meaning.
levels.Extending: Makes the change and chooses words that make the sentence stronger than the original.

levels.Beginning: Writes the sentence with three or more mistakes of spelling, grammar or punctuation.
levels.Developing: Writes the sentence with one or two mistakes.
levels.Secure: Writes the sentence with no mistakes in the words and marks asked for.
levels.Extending: Writes the sentence with no mistakes and uses a mark or word beyond the brief correctly.

rubrics.name: A short piece of writing
rubrics.applies_to: ENG.SHORT_WRITE: describing, telling events, a profile, a new ending

levels.Beginning: With help, writes one or two sentences on the topic.
levels.Developing: Writes on the topic but leaves out a part the task asked for.
levels.Secure: Writes every part the task asked for, with at least two chosen details.
levels.Extending: Writes every part with details that would surprise or interest a reader.

levels.Beginning: Writes ideas in an order that is hard to follow.
levels.Developing: Writes ideas in order, linked only by and or then.
levels.Secure: Writes ideas in a clear order and links them with at least two different linking words.
levels.Extending: Orders ideas so each builds on the last, with links chosen for time, cause or contrast.

levels.Beginning: Uses mostly general words (nice, good, went).
levels.Developing: Uses one or two chosen words, such as a describing word or a strong verb.
levels.Secure: Uses chosen words in most sentences: describing words, strong verbs or senses.
levels.Extending: Uses chosen words and one comparison, such as a simile, that fits the piece.

levels.Beginning: Writes sentences that run together, with few capitals or full stops.
levels.Developing: Writes most sentences with a capital and an end mark; three or more slips.
levels.Secure: Writes sentences with capitals and end marks; at most two slips of spelling or grammar.
levels.Extending: Writes varied sentences, including one with two clauses, with at most one slip.

criteria.name: Sets it out as a playscript

levels.Beginning: Writes the lines as a story, with speech marks.
levels.Developing: Writes speakers' names, but misses colons or new lines for some speakers.
levels.Secure: Writes each speaker's name, a colon and their words on a new line, with no speech marks.
levels.Extending: Sets it out correctly and adds a scene heading and a list of characters.

levels.Developing: Writes one stage direction, but not in brackets or not in the present tense.
levels.Secure: Writes at least two stage directions in brackets, in the present tense.
levels.Extending: Writes stage directions that show feeling or movement the lines do not say.

levels.Beginning: Writes lines that do not follow the story or the brief.
levels.Developing: Writes lines that follow the brief, but a narrator would be needed to follow them.
levels.Secure: Writes lines from which a listener can follow what happens.
levels.Extending: Writes lines that also show each character's personality.

rubrics.name: A view, opinion or review
rubrics.applies_to: ENG.SHORT_WRITE: a review, a character's opinion, a view for a reader

levels.Beginning: Writes about the topic without saying what they, or the character, think.
levels.Developing: States a view, but it changes or is unclear by the end.
levels.Secure: States one clear view at the start and keeps to it.
levels.Extending: States a clear view and answers one point someone might make against it.

levels.Secure: Gives two reasons, each with a detail or an example.
levels.Extending: Gives two or more reasons with details and says which matters most.

levels.Beginning: Writes in a way that does not suit the reader named in the task.
levels.Developing: Writes mostly for the reader, with a slip in tone, such as being too casual.
levels.Secure: Writes for the reader named, with a fitting greeting, tone and ending.
levels.Extending: Writes for the reader and chooses words likely to persuade or interest that reader.

rubrics.name: A plan or notes
rubrics.applies_to: ENG.SHORT_WRITE and ENG.TABLE: a plan, notes from a text

levels.Beginning: Records one point, or points that do not fit the task.
levels.Developing: Records some main points but leaves one out.
levels.Secure: Records every main point the task or text needs.
levels.Extending: Records every main point and marks which matters most.

levels.Beginning: Copies whole sentences or writes a full story.
levels.Developing: Writes some points as short notes and some as long sentences.
levels.Secure: Writes each point as a short note of a few key words.
levels.Extending: Writes short notes and uses symbols or arrows to show links.

criteria.name: Puts points in an order to write from

levels.Beginning: Writes points in no clear order.
levels.Developing: Writes points in order, but one is out of place.
levels.Secure: Writes points in the order they would be written up.
levels.Extending: Writes points in order and groups them as paragraphs or sections.

rubrics.name: Improving a piece of writing
rubrics.applies_to: ENG.SHORT_ANSWER and ENG.REWRITE: suggesting and making an improvement

levels.Beginning: Names a change that would not improve the writing.
levels.Developing: Names a general change, such as 'add more detail', without saying where.
levels.Secure: Names one exact place to improve and what is weak there.
levels.Extending: Names the place, what is weak and why it matters to the reader.

levels.Beginning: Writes no new version, or one with the same weakness.
levels.Developing: Writes a new version that is a little better but adds a new mistake.
levels.Secure: Writes a new version that fixes the weakness with no new mistakes.
levels.Extending: Writes a new version that fixes it and makes the passage more interesting to read.
